newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian linear bonds seen in tight range.
newsitem.headline: Belgian linear bonds seen in tight range.

text.p: Belgian linear bonds are seen in narrow ranges for the rest of the week, as investors refuse to buy OLOs at the current low yield levels and the stable budget outlook is keeping sellers at bay.

The June OLO future contract, which expired today, closed two bp higher at 122.28 after rising to 122.45, while the September contract ended 18 bp higher at 121.04 after rising to 121.15. Volume in both was tiny, with just 45 lots traded in the June contract and 206 in the September one.
Traders said the lack of volume in the past weeks was hurting primary dealers and brokers.
"U.S. GDP data on Friday should give some impetus to trading, but I would not bank on it," one dealer said.
Dealers said the market's atttention had started to focus on the 1998 budget, due to be drafted after the summer.

A report by Belgium's authoritative High Finance Council on Tuesday recommended Belgium cut its deficit to 2.3 percent, more than the 2.5 percent put forward in the government's three-year budget plan laid down in October 1996.
But most players said the budget did not worry them, as Belgium's budget deficit looked small by comparison to France and Germany.
But one added that Belgium had to do better on the deficit front as its debt to GDP ratio, at about 130 percent of GDP is the worst in Europe.
-- Geert De Clercq, Brussels Newsroom +32 2 287 6813, Fax +32 2 230 7710
